outline.chapter_title: Motivation and Challenges in Scaling Large Language Models
outline.description: This chapter introduces the rapid growth of LLMs, their performance benefits, and the practical challenges they pose in terms of memory footprint, latency, energy consumption, and environmental impact.
subtopics: Historical progress from early language models to modern multi-billion-parameter transformers
Why model size matters: performance vs compute trade‑offs
Hardware bottlenecks in inference—memory bandwidth, DRAM↔SRAM transfers
Energy consumption patterns of floating‑point arithmetic on modern silicon
Economic and ecological motivations for more efficient inference

outline.chapter_title: Foundations of Model Quantization for Neural Networks
outline.description: A systematic overview of numerical precision in deep learning models, focusing on why quantization is an effective tool for reducing inference cost.
subtopics: Floating‑point formats (FP16/BF16) versus integer formats
Post‑training quantization (PTQ) versus quantization‑aware training (QAT)
Common low‑bit schemes: 8‑bit uniform quantization, 4‑bit techniques (SmoothQuant, GPTQ)
Impact of quantization on accuracy and hardware efficiency
Limitations of PTQ when applied to very large language models

outline.chapter_title: Binary and Ternary Neural Networks: Theory and Benefits
outline.description: Explores extreme low‑bit representations—binary {−1,+1} and ternary {−1,0,+1}—and explains the mathematical rationale behind using only ~1 bit per weight.
subtopics: (a) Information content calculation leading to the 1.58‑bit figure
(b) Role of the zero value as an implicit feature filter/sparsity promoter
(c) Prior work on binarized networks in computer vision and NLP
(d) Advantages in arithmetic energy cost when multiplications disappear
(e) Potential downsides such as reduced representational capacity

outline.description: Describes the predecessor BitNet that introduced a fully integer matrix multiplication pipeline by replacing standard linear layers with BitLinear.
subtopics: Standard Transformer components relevant to BitNet
BitLinear layer implementation details—integer addition only matrix multiplication
Training pipeline used in the original BitNet paper
Observed speedup and memory savings compared with FP16 baselines
Limitations that motivated the development of a ternary variant

outline.chapter_title: Designing BitNet b1.58: Ternary Weights and Activation Strategies
outline.description: In depth coverage of the novel contributions that define BitNet b1.58—including its ternary weight quantizer, activation handling, and adoption of LLaMA‑style components.
subtopics: "AbsMean" weight quantizer formulation:
- Scaling by average absolute value \(\gamma\)
- RoundClip operation mapping weights to \{-1,0,+1\}
- Mathematical derivation of \(\gamma = \frac{1}{nm}\sum_{ij}|W_{ij}|\)
"Activation quantization": unsigned versus signed range \([-Q_b,Q_b]\)
"LLaMA-alike" backbone changes:
- RMSNorm instead of LayerNorm
- SwiGLU activation function
- Rotary positional embeddings (RoPE)
- Removal of bias terms for hardware simplicity
"Integration pathways": compatibility with HuggingFace Transformers, vLLM and llama.cpp
